thread:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up re: telemetry prefetching + shard routing. TL;DR: we need to pick an approach for parallelism (per-shard prefetch vs shared prefetcher with leasing). Concerns: cost, ordering, idempotency, and cost attribution.

michael: i'm leaning toward per-shard prefetch for simplicity. each consumer keeps a small ring buffer and we avoid cross-shard coordination. easier to reason about backpressure. :thinking_face:

samir: per-shard sounds simpler but we blow up memory and duplicate effort on hot tenants. what's the expected peak buffer size per shard? and how does that surface in cost dashboards?

anya: good q. rough calc: buffer ~128KB per active tenant per shard in our PoC. at scale that matters. shared prefetch + lease can amortize memory but adds complexity (lease holder crash, rebalancing, lease storms).

lucy: also think about cost attribution — if we share a prefetcher across tenants, we need deterministic billing keys on the outgoing envelope otherwise we lose per-tenant cost split. that's an extra enrichment step before batching.

kai: ordering/consistency: if a shared prefetcher merges streams, we need to preserve per-tenant ordering for traces. If we use batch-windowing we may reorder across sources unless we pin per-tenant sequence stamps. Adds more state.

michael: what about hybrid: keep small per-shard hot buffers for top N tenants (by recent qps) + a shared prefetcher for the long tail. that matches our cost profile (80/20).

anya: hybrid seems promising. couple follow-ups: 1) how do we elect hot tenants? LRU over a sliding window? 2) how to fall back on lease failure? 3) how to surface cost attribution in metrics immediately (no eventual join)?

samir: for (1) sliding-window LRU + size threshold. we already have a lightweight recent-qps counter in the gateway. export that as a scored metric and pick top-N per shard every minute.

lucy: for (3) we should attach billing_key earlier at gateway so any prefetcher emits envelopes with billing_key set. that avoids a late join. small caveat: billing_key resolution requires tenant metadata lookup; we can cache it in the gateway.

kai: for (2) lease failure fallback: when lease owner misses heartbeat, other worker can claim, but we must rehydrate the hot buffer state. require idempotent fetches from source (cursor based). keep fetch cursors in durable kv so rehydration doesn't double-send.

observability-bot: deploy-check: staging prefetcher build passed (ci/obs-prefetcher #1182). :white_check_mark:

michael: benchmark note: PoC numbers — per-shard buffers (128KB * 1k tenants) = 128MB, approx 8-10% memory overhead on our worker class. shared prefetcher with 1MB aggregate buffer cuts mem by ~60% but CPU for coordination + lease heartbeats went up ~12%.

anya: given numbers, hybrid wins if top-N << total tenants. but we need safety for hotspots shifting quickly. suggest shorter sampling window (30s) for hotness and a gentle migration (draining + copying cache) when a tenant loses hot status.

samir: can we instrument migration cost as a metric (prefetch.migrations.count, prefetch.migrations.duration, prefetch.migrations.dropped_events)? we should alert if migrations spike.

lucy: also add trace tags: prefetch.method={per-shard,shared,hybrid}, prefetch.leader={node-id}, billing_key. so evals and cost dashboards can slice by method.

kai: edge case: heavy fanout tenant (many parallel sequence streams). hot-buffer per-shard might saturate. we should detect fanout by unique stream-key cardinality and route heavy fanout tenants to dedicated workers (special pool) rather than typical hot cache.

anya: agrees. add policy: if unique-stream-keys > 1000 in last 1m, mark for dedicated pool.

michael: rollout plan idea: canary on 5% of traffic with hybrid mode enabled, weighted selection per-tenant (prefer mid-size tenants), monitor migrations, errors, memory, latencies.

anya: action items:
- michael: sketch hybrid prefetcher design + breakpoints for N and buffer sizes (due EOD Friday)
- kai: sketch rehydrate flow + durable cursor contract (due Tue)
- lucy: list billing_key caching requirements and where to attach (gateway vs prefetcher) (due Wed)
- samir: define migration metrics and add dashboards/alerts (due Wed)

michael: quick config snippet idea for hybrid thresholds:
```yaml
prefetch:
  hot_window_sec: 30
  hot_top_n: 200
  per_shard_buffer_bytes: 131072 # 128KB
  shared_aggregate_bytes: 1048576 # 1MB
  dedicated_fanout_threshold: 1000
```

lucy: ^ looks good. also add billing_key_cache_ttl and cache_max_entries.

anya: cool. if no objections i'll put a short RFC addendum with these choices + canary plan and link to this thread. thanks all. :rocket:

kai: :+1: let's sync if PoC data changes.

samir: thanks, good tradeoff call.

observability-bot: reminder: add RFC link to PR description when you open the addendum.
